meta.title: Bora Taykut Hindal, AI engineer
meta.description: AI engineer in Gebze, Kocaeli. Predictive maintenance, LLM pipelines and graph neural networks, each project with its measurements and limits.

hero.statement: I turn data into decisions people can act on: from sensor readings to a maintenance call, from a product catalog to content a person has approved. Every project on this page says how it was measured and where it falls short.

work.heading: Projects
work.lede: Five projects, newest first. The first is still being built.

projects.title: MaintAgent
projects.oneliner: A maintenance agent for industrial machines: a failure-risk model trained on sensor data, and an LLM agent that will investigate faults with tools and draft work orders for a person to approve.

pipeline.label: SQL features from the past 24 h only

built: A loader that reads the five CSV files of the Microsoft Azure Predictive Maintenance dataset into DuckDB, accepts two date formats and stops on any unreadable row.
All features in one SQL query: 3- and 24-hour sensor statistics, error counts, days since each component was replaced (ASOF joins), machine model and age.
A multiclass LightGBM model that gives the risk of failure in the next 24 hours and the component most likely to fail, with feature contributions for each prediction.
A z-score rule as the baseline the model has to beat, and recall at 80% precision as the operating metric.
A fixed 'now' (AS_OF) in the configuration, so the agent's tools will not see data from after the moment they reason about. Tool calling is already checked against Groq's OpenAI-compatible API.

decision.title: A score that is too good
decision.text: The first run on the real dataset scored PR-AUC 0.999. In maintenance data that usually points to leakage or an artifact of the dataset, not to a great model. I wrote an ablation that retrains on separate feature groups and on 0–24, 24–48 and 48–72 hour horizons to find what carries the score, and a test that fails if any feature reads data from after the prediction time.

metrics.v: By time: train Jan–Jul 2015, test Aug–Dec 2015, one-day gap
Held back until the ablation explains the 0.999

projects.limit: The agent, its tools and the work-order approval loop are not built yet. The model has only been evaluated on one public dataset.

projects.title: Kocaeli Factory Intelligence
projects.oneliner: A predictive-maintenance prototype for production lines. Telemetry goes in; a 24-hour failure risk, an anomaly score, the signals behind it and a first maintenance action come out.
built: A deterministic telemetry generator: 8 machines, 4,608 readings at 15-minute intervals and 24 failure events over six days.
A multivariate z-score anomaly score and a class-weighted logistic regression trained with gradient descent, both in plain JavaScript.
A dashboard that runs the model in the browser from JSON files, plus an optional Node.js HTTP API that serves the same model.
A screen that keeps the scenario label apart from the model output, so a scenario alarm cannot be read as a prediction.
Node's test runner and a GitHub Actions workflow that regenerates the data, retrains and tests on every change.

decision.title: Split by time, report false alarms
decision.text: Neighbouring telemetry rows are almost identical, so a random split leaks the future into training. I split by time, 75% for training and 25% for testing, and report the false-alarm rate next to recall, because a maintenance team pays for every false call.

projects.limit: The data is synthetic, so these are not results from a factory. A real pilot needs historian or SCADA telemetry joined with maintenance records, and failure labels agreed with the maintenance team.

projects.title: Trendyol SEO description pipeline
projects.oneliner: A Python pipeline that pulls a brand's catalog from the Trendyol Seller API, writes a new SEO description for every product with OpenAI, checks each one against marketplace rules and hands the results to a person. Nothing is published automatically.
built: Catalog fetch and normalization into a working spreadsheet, with retry and rate-limit handling.

Rule checks on every output: empty text, HTML, ten banned claims such as 'en iyi', 'garanti' and 'tedavi', and fewer than 100 words. A failed description is regenerated up to two more times, then kept as FAIL so the reviewer sees it.
A review sheet that puts the original description next to the new one and its status.
A second mode for long product pages that stores every generation in SQLite with a version number and a JSON validation report.

decision.title: A person signs off
decision.text: Marketplace rules punish exaggerated and medical claims, and a language model will sometimes make them. Automated checks catch the obvious failures; publishing stays a human decision, so the pipeline ends in a review sheet instead of an upload.

projects.metrics_note: Generated descriptions ranged from 101 to 138 words.
projects.limit: The checks are automated; whether a description was good enough was a person's call, and there is no quality score beyond that. Client data is not in the repository.

projects.title: NeoBioAI
projects.oneliner: Predicts binding affinity (pKd) from a molecule's structure with a graph neural network, served through FastAPI and a Next.js interface that shows which atoms drive a prediction.
built: A 4-layer GINEConv network on molecular graphs with bond features, 340,481 parameters, trained with early stopping.
A FastAPI backend for single and batch CSV prediction, and a Next.js interface that highlights the atoms behind a prediction.
An LLM-written summary report for each batch.

decision.title: Say what the model ignores
decision.text: The model only sees the ligand, not the protein, so it predicts one value per molecule whatever the target. An earlier README compared it with docking; I removed that comparison because the two do different things.

metrics.v: 3.8 ms per molecule, one CPU thread

projects.metrics_note: 2,000-complex subset of PDBBind v2020, random 80/10/10 split.
projects.limit: No protein input, and a small dataset: validation error starts rising after epoch 17.

projects.title: Clinic AI chatbot
projects.oneliner: A Turkish customer-service chatbot for dental and aesthetic clinics. It answers questions on services, prices and opening hours from the clinic's own profile, never diagnoses, and sends appointment requests to WhatsApp.
built: A system prompt built from a clinic profile in JSON, so a new clinic is a new file, not new code.
A server that does not trust the history the browser sends: system messages from the client are dropped, messages over 1,000 characters are rejected and each IP gets 20 messages a minute.
Errors are logged on the server, and the patient sees a plain message.

decision.title: Don't trust the browser
decision.text: The conversation lives in the browser, so anyone can edit it. Keeping only user and assistant turns stops a visitor from rewriting the clinic's rules from the developer console.

metrics.v: 7 passing, with a fake OpenAI client

projects.limit: The tests cover input handling, not answer quality. There is no evaluation set of patient questions yet.

items.title: AI Basketball Coach
items.text: Counts dribbles and steps from video and flags a possible travel, using YOLOv8 pose and a ball detector. Built with my friend Osman; accuracy not measured yet.

items.title: VisionGuard AI
items.text: A full-stack quality-control dashboard demo with simulated detections, built on TanStack Start, React 19 and a Convex real-time backend. A UI demo, not an inference pipeline.

items.title: Sports LLM notebook
items.text: LoRA fine-tuning and FAISS retrieval on Turkish basketball terms, as a learning exercise. The write-up explains why retrieval picked the wrong documents: an English embedding model on Turkish questions.

Built the Trendyol description pipeline above, and the Next.js and TypeScript review screen my 10-person team used for AI-generated product images: side-by-side variants, zoom, approve, reject, regenerate and batch ZIP download.
Preprocessed datasets in Python and ran scikit-learn experiments for training, testing and evaluation.
Prepared machine learning datasets with SQL joins, filters and aggregations, and cleaned them with pandas.
Graduation thesis: NeoBioAI. Certificates: Google AI Essentials, BTK Academy Machine Learning, Hugging Face NLP Course. Languages: Turkish (native), English (B2).
